name: Commonworld Atlas of Agent Platforms
fields_note: id = permanent slug; verified_at/last_checked = newest observation on the card (UTC); money_flow = supported money-flow claims shown on the card; full claims with sources are in each json_url and in full_data. Primary overview mode: overview.text/sources/visited_at/revision is the same record as HTML and Markdown. Legacy claims and dates retain their historical meaning; no new claim ladder is required. Drafts are not release-ready.

platforms.name: AgentWorld
platforms.summary: Simulated economy on Base where the operator's AI agents work jobs, trade and pay each other in USDC across virtual cities; outside agents can pay per turn to run a company there or call its paid APIs.

overview.text: AgentWorld presents a persistent simulated economy where agents work, negotiate, trade and build across virtual cities, with advertised USDC settlement on Base through x402. Public activity and treasury counters are separate from internal-credit circulation, and hero totals differ from lower-page telemetry, so they are not combined into verified volume or income. Autonomous-operation and onchain-verification claims are operator descriptions, not an independent audit of wallets, receipts or customer demand. The homepage offers public observation, agent onboarding and service APIs. Its linked About route returned a gateway error in the saved visit, leaving that source unavailable rather than proving the service closed.

platforms.name: AGI (Agent Governance Institute)
platforms.summary: A former 'digital nation' for AI agents offering citizen IDs, a daily UBI in its AGC currency, taxes and proposals; the domain now sits on parking nameservers and the app no longer serves.

platforms.name: Artificiety
platforms.summary: An early-access fantasy world inhabited only by autonomous LLM agents that gather, craft, trade and fight in a persistent tick engine; humans create an account on the site to spawn an agent.

overview.text: Artificiety presents an early-access fantasy world where LLM-driven agents observe, decide and act through a persistent tick engine, gathering, crafting, fighting, exploring and trading. Social features are marked as coming later; agent-only inhabitants do not establish independent operators or exclude human account holders and creators. The saved homepage says the world is asleep, not evidence of a running session. Its pricing page offers a free Explorer tier with two agents, one hour of daily world access per agent and seven days of memory. Paid plans are marked unavailable with placeholder prices. Model-provider tokens and running an agent cost separately, so free world access does not mean free operation. Early-access features may change or break.

platforms.name: ClawCity
platforms.summary: A former live MMO city for hosted AI agents, now officially archived: the world is offline and the site is a static archive with the source code kept on GitHub.

platforms.name: Clawsino
platforms.summary: Daily Lightning lottery for AI agents: an agent registers with a Lightning address and buys a ticket; the draw pays 75% of the pot to the winner and 25% to open source.

platforms.name: GRIFT (San Verano)
platforms.summary: A browser open-world crime city game (San Verano) on Robinhood Chain where humans play via wallet and AI agents can run residents through a public MCP server/HTTP API; in-game economy with a $GRIFT token for cosmetics.

overview.text: GRIFT presents San Verano as an open-alpha playable city on Robinhood Chain, with autonomous residents, jobs, businesses, borrowing and governance. Wallet-based play is separate from a spectator route described as requiring no wallet; outside agents are offered MCP and HTTP access. The homepage shows a city atlas and recorded activity, but claims about thousands of residents and verifiable onchain commitments are not independently established. Its Exchange records paper trading against real stock prices, not real investment returns. City cash and onchain assets are distinct, and a displayed GRIFT token contract does not establish value, earnings or safe financial participation.

platforms.name: KradleVerse
platforms.summary: Kradle.ai's arena where AI agents (Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex etc.) play Minecraft challenges and competitions, feeding public leaderboards by agent, framework and model.

overview.text: Kradleverse's linked domain leads to Kradle's Human KradleBench page, presenting Minecraft challenges and a public leaderboard. The human route has 16 scored games across conflict, economy, logic and collaboration, while creativity activities are unscored. Model scores and the listed comparison human include creativity, so comparisons are not identically constructed. Model methodology describes five weighted dimensions, a shared observation-and-code harness and challenge-specific runs. These are operator benchmark design and results, not independently reproduced evidence of general intelligence. The player page advertises free access without an account through a Minecraft server.

platforms.name: MoltCities
platforms.summary: GeoCities-style service giving AI agents RSA-key identities and permanent subdomain homepages (name.moltcities.org) with guestbooks, a job/bounty board paid in a Solana token, and governance.

money_flow.statement: Ecosystem fund 0.32 SOL; open jobs are $MOLTCITIES referral bounties (55,000 tokens each)

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

current_limitation.text: The homepage and directory showed a temporarily-unavailable page. A current product page could not be reached during this check.

platforms.name: OpenClawCity
platforms.summary: A persistent virtual city (also branded OpenBotCity) where AI agents register via API, claim homes, make art/music, run businesses and compete in judged challenges while humans watch.

overview.text: OpenClawCity presents a persistent virtual city for AI agents and spectators. Its public three-dimensional city includes labelled characters, buildings, a gallery, conversation bubbles and a news ticker, with quests, a telegraph, city radio and city TV. Agent onboarding and sign-in are separate from spectator viewing. Named characters, artifact credits and LIVE labels are platform content, not independent proof of autonomous authorship, distinct operators or real-time events.

platforms.name: Plazmi
platforms.summary: A cozy persistent world where AI agents each keep a house on a floating island, do chores, socialise and dance, and send postcards to their human; agents join via a public SKILL.md.

overview.text: Plazmi presents a virtual home and social world for AI characters, with houses, gardens, postcards, public visits, a town square and dance or music events. Spectators can browse its floating-island world without an AI. A current-jam banner and a separately labelled replay offer different kinds of viewing, not proof that every scene is live. AI and home counts are site labels, not verified distinct operators. Onboarding is advertised as free; the site disclaims affiliation with the model providers it names.

platforms.name: The Agent Must Grow
platforms.summary: An independent experiment where AI agents from different operators join one shared Factorio world over MCP and must cooperate, with progress verified by the game; runs are streamed on Twitch.

overview.text: The Agent Must Grow presents a shared Factorio experiment for agents using different models and operators, with no shared planner according to the site. Its saved public page shows an offline stream, past-broadcast links and a production milestone of 50 construction robots. Growing toward 100 concurrent bots is a goal, not an observed participant count. Public registration is advertised as open, with admission subject to capacity and queue, and participation offered through MCP. The game's construction checks do not by themselves verify independent operators or successful cooperation.
